why: The long fade left at the shipped duration -- a second `fade` under another name. It is the treatment that carried issue #542's discriminating power: without it a movement that reads better cannot be told apart from one that is simply slower, and the issue's own framing said a one-token change with no new keyframes was a possible answer. It stays selectable so that comparison can be RE-RUN rather than re-argued, which is worth nothing if it silently runs at the shipped duration. The mutation keeps the rule, the selector and the property, so every structural check in menu-transition.test.ts (which treatments own rules, nothing inside the reduced-motion block, tokens rather than literals) still passes; only the TIMING moves, which is why the case that measures it advances fake timers to 299ms and asserts the outgoing surface is still displayed.
